- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.2) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overreacts and forecasts continued rise; cap forecast at +1–2% above peak or apply mean reversion to prior 5-day average.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model often fails to adjust; force a 3–5 day lagged mean reversion correction.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 5 days.
- When sentiment is flat (0.0–0.2) and price is near historical mean, model tends to forecast mean-reversion too aggressively; reduce forecast volatility by 20–30%.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion within 7–10 days after a spike, model often fails to recognize it; apply a 3–5 day smoothing filter to forecast.
